answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and burns one 50-credit ferrous token, an irreversible burn emitting a signal receipt bound to its key and recorded in the river ledger. An auditor replays the river ledger and burns the bond for a reused or key-mismatched receipt. A rented-token ring fails: lending a token for burning destroys the lender's asset, so no token serves two identities. The k-th fake needs a fresh token and bond, a marginal 110 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and burn 50,000. An honest identity pays 50 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
